name: pixelbolt
description: Pixel art and sprite animation for agents: JSON recipes to PNG, APNG, GIF and sprite sheets.
long_description: Create, inspect and revise pixel art from editable JSON recipes. Export sprites, animations, atlases and scenes with eight local MCP tools. The server makes no network requests. Choose a workspace for local recipe references and generated artwork.

tools.name: pixel_help
tools.description: Start here before drawing pixel art: a short quick start, with the full guide, schemas and a complete editable example as topics.

tools.name: pixel_validate
tools.description: Check a pixel art recipe for mistakes, report dimensions and timing, and save an immutable revision.

tools.name: pixel_inspect
tools.description: Look at a sprite or animation frame by frame: contact sheets, palette-key grids and optional diagnostics.

tools.name: pixel_patch
tools.description: Fix one pixel, a colour or a frame with targeted edits, corrections or overlays, and compare the result.

tools.name: pixel_render
tools.description: Export sprite sheets, atlases, animations, GIFs, video frames and a Canvas player into a new unique folder, and images, atlases and recipes at paths you name.

tools.name: pixel_compile
tools.description: Build character animations from poses, terrain tilesets, particle effects, simulated smoke, fire and water, or lighting normal passes as editable recipes.

tools.name: pixel_scene
tools.description: Compose and render a scene or room from sprites and tilemaps, with optional scene or frame exports.

tools.name: pixel_import
tools.description: Turn existing pixel art (an 8-bit RGB/RGBA PNG) into an editable recipe without changing its pixels.

workspace.title: Workspace
workspace.description: Folder Pixelbolt reads recipe and PNG references from. When you ask for a file by name, Pixelbolt saves that image, atlas or recipe here too (never under a hidden name or in AppData or Library, and replacing a file only when you say so). Renders and revisions go in its Pixelbolt subfolder, created on first use. Choose a project folder to keep its files together.
